problem: Let $\pi:Y\rightarrow \mathbb{P}^3$ be the blow-up of two points $p,q\in\mathbb{P}^3$, and then of the strict transform of the line $L$ spanned by them. Let $E_p,E_q, E_{p,q}$ be the exceptional divisors over $p,q$, and $L$, respectively. $E_p$ and $E_q$ are isomorphic to the blow-up of a point in $\mathbb{P}^2$, and $E_{p,q}\cong \mathbb{P}^1\times\mathbb{P}^1$. Let $\sigma_{p,q}\subset E_{p,q}$ be the class of the $\mathbb{P}^1$ which is not contracted by $\pi$. Given that $E_p\cdot \sigma_{p,q} = E_q\cdot\sigma_{p,q} = 1$, find the intersection number $E_{p,q}\cdot \sigma_{p,q}$. Provide your answer as a single number.

answer_text:
Looking at this problem, I need to find the intersection number $E_{p,q} \cdot \sigma_{p,q}$ where $\sigma_{p,q}$ is the section of the $\mathbb{P}^1$-bundle $E_{p,q} \to L$ that is **not** contracted by $\pi$.

## Setting Up the Normal Bundle

First, I determine the normal bundle of the strict transform of $L$ in the 3-fold $X = \text{Bl}_{p,q}(\mathbb{P}^3)$.

The line $L \cong \mathbb{P}^1$ in $\mathbb{P}^3$ has normal bundle $N_{L/\mathbb{P}^3} = \mathcal{O}(1) \oplus \mathcal{O}(1)$.

Blowing up a smooth point of a curve in a 3-fold subtracts one from the degree of the normal bundle. After blowing up both $p$ and $q$ on $L$:
$$N_{\tilde{L}/X} = \mathcal{O}(-1) \oplus \mathcal{O}(-1)$$

## Verifying $E_{p,q} \cong \mathbb{P}^1 \times \mathbb{P}^1$

The exceptional divisor $E_{p,q} = \mathbb{P}(N_{\tilde{L}/X}) = \mathbb{P}(\mathcal{O}(-1) \oplus \mathcal{O}(-1)) = \mathbb{P}(\mathcal{O} \oplus \mathcal{O}) \cong \mathbb{P}^1 \times \mathbb{P}^1$ ✓

## Computing the Intersection

The key formula: for a curve $C \subset E$ where $E$ is the exceptional divisor of a blow-up along a curve with normal bundle $N$,
$$E \cdot C = \deg\bigl(\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}(N)}(-1)\big|_C\bigr)$$

The tautological bundle on $\mathbb{P}^1 \times \mathbb{P}^1$ decomposes as:
$$\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}(N)}(-1) = \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^1 \times \mathbb{P}^1}(-1,-1)$$

where the first $(-1)$ comes from the base direction (from the $\mathcal{O}(-1)$ factor of $N$) and the second $(-1)$ is the fiberwise tautological.

**Restricting to the section $\sigma_{p,q}$:** A section $\sigma \cong \mathbb{P}^1$ maps to the base $\mathbb{P}^1$ isomorphically. Restricting $\mathcal{O}(-1,-1)$ to $\sigma$:
$$\mathcal{O}(-1,-1)\big|_\sigma = \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^1}(-1)$$

Therefore:
$$E_{p,q} \cdot \sigma_{p,q} = \deg\bigl(\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^1}(-1)\bigr) = -1$$

## Consistency Check

The given data confirms our setup:
- $\sigma_{p,q}$ meets the fiber of $E_{p,q} \to \tilde{L}$ over the point where $\tilde{L} \cap E_p$ at exactly one point, giving $E_p \cdot \sigma_{p,q} = 1$ ✓
- Similarly $E_q \cdot \sigma_{p,q} = 1$ ✓
- The fiber class (contracted by $\pi$) would give $E_{p,q} \cdot f = -1$ as well, consistent with the standard exceptional divisor formula.

$$\boxed{-1}$$
